one_liner: Mid-to-senior budget analyst at NGA, reviewing, justifying and tracking agency spending through the defense Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) cycle.
fit_summary: Daniel's background as known is in emergency-management consulting, policy knowledge and relationship-building, not budget analysis. This Band 4 role requires demonstrated experience evaluating budget estimates, recommending on funds requests and using financial systems, plus a degree, a degree-and-experience combination or 4 years of finance-related experience. Daniel would be competitive only if the IEM work involved substantial budget, grant or cost analysis that can be documented.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens). No federal status is needed, and veterans' preference applies only if you are eligible, which Daniel is not.

Must meet all five Mandatory Qualification Criteria, which cover budget execution analysis, evaluating estimates and funds requests, responding to budget inquiries, recommending corrective actions, and using financial databases and spreadsheets.

Education/experience option: a bachelor's in Accounting, Business, Finance, Public Administration or a related field; or 24 semester hours in those fields plus experience totaling 4 years; or 4 years of accounting, budget or financial analysis experience.
You must be able to obtain a Top Secret/SCI clearance and pass a counterintelligence polygraph and a drug test. You will also file an annual SF-714 financial disclosure.
strategy: First, inventory honestly whether your IEM work involved project budgets, FEMA Public Assistance or grant cost estimates, reimbursement reviews or burn-rate tracking. If it did not, this posting is not worth the effort and similar non-budget roles are a better use of your time.

If it did, frame the IEM experience in budget language, for example: reviewed cost estimates for disaster recovery projects, recommended approval or disapproval of reimbursement requests, and tracked spending against deliverable timelines.

Write one resume entry for each of the five mandatory criteria, using specific examples with results as the posting demands. Include hours per week and dates, and keep it within the 2-page NGA resume builder limit.

Check your degree field. A Public Administration or political science degree with relevant business or finance coursework may count under option A or B, so list your degree and coursework hours explicitly.
Add a short optional cover letter connecting your policy fluency to defending budget justifications to stakeholders.
Apply between Oct 19 and Oct 31, 2026, and expect a clearance process that may take a year or more.
resume_bullets: Reviewed [number] cost estimates/funding requests totaling $[amount] for [government client] disaster recovery projects and recommended [approval/adjustments] based on [eligibility rules/regulations].

Tracked budget execution for [project/contract] in [Excel/system], reporting spend versus deliverable timelines to [client/manager] [frequency] and flagging [issue] with corrective actions that [result].
Drafted responses to [number] budget-related inquiries from [client staff/auditors], coordinating with [teams] to resolve [type of financial issue].
interview_questions: Walk us through a time you evaluated a budget estimate or funds request and made a recommendation.
How have you tracked budget execution and handled a program that was under- or over-executing?
Describe how you explained a complex financial issue to a non-financial stakeholder.
What spreadsheets or financial systems have you used, and how did you present findings visually?
watch_outs: The mandatory criteria require real budget-analysis experience, and emergency-management or policy work alone will not qualify.
Requires TS/SCI clearance and a polygraph. The process is lengthy and the job is on-site only with no telework.
Under NGA's mobility model, the actual assignment and location are unknown until after clearance.
Short window: the posting is open only Oct 19–31, 2026.
